description: Working in-place two pointer swap in C, but confused on pointer arithmetic vs array indexing.

transcript.text: Please reverse an array of characters in-place.
I will use two pointers, start at 0 and end at length - 1, and swap until they meet.
How do you do the swap in C?
Using a temp char variable: char tmp = s[i]; s[i] = s[j]; s[j] = tmp;
Maybe O(n) because of the string size? Or O(1)?
Auxiliary space is only the extra memory allocated.
Oh right, then O(1) auxiliary space.
